chapter_note: This is the foundational hagiographic chapter of the Kephalaia — overwhelmingly editorial. The chapter title 'Concerning the Advent of the Apostle' announces its purpose: to establish Mani's apostolic credentials within a succession (Sethel→Enoch→Shem→Buddha→Aurentes→Zarathustra→Jesus→Mani), to identify Mani as the Paraclete, and to recount his autobiography (revelation at age of perfection, missions to India and Persia under Shapur). The farmer parable (i=0-34) and tree parable (i=59-71) are correspondential in FORM but used as editorial vehicles for the apostolic-succession theme. The Jesus narrative (i=92-115) brings in NT material with anti-Jewish polemic. Genuine substrate content surfaces only briefly in i=173-185 where Mani summarizes the cosmological mysteries revealed to him by the Paraclete — Light/Darkness, the war, the joining drawing into world, the ships refining Light, the molding of Adam, the Tree of Knowledge. Even there, the framing 'He revealed to me X' is editorial; only the cosmic-content phrases inside are substratic. Teaching purity of 0.078 is exceptionally low and reflects the chapter's editorial function as preface/credentials.
